title: Trump Rallies in South Carolina as Senate Race Tightens Days Before Midterms
dek: President Trump campaigned for Republican candidates in Rock Hill on Thursday, as Sen. Darline Graham's race against Democrat Annie Andrews tightened and Democrats raised concerns about his stance on the election results.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The west front of the United States Capitol building in Washington, D.C., where Congress convenes after the midterm elections

keyPoints: Trump spoke at a campaign rally at the Rock Hill Sports & Event Center in Rock Hill, S.C., on Thursday, Oct. 29, supporting South Carolina Republicans, including Sen. Darline Graham.
Fox News reported that Graham's race against Democrat Annie Andrews has tightened, prompting Trump's return to the state; the same day he also campaigned in Ohio.

Trump repeated claims of voter fraud in Alaska's Senate race and called for Democratic candidate Mary Peltola to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted; those claims are the president's and have not been established by a court.
Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., said Democrats are concerned Trump may not accept next week's midterm results, a claim Meridian has not independently verified.
body:
President Donald Trump spoke at a campaign rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina, on Thursday, backing Republican candidates ahead of next week's midterm elections. The Charlotte Observer reported from the Rock Hill Sports & Event Center, where supporters waited in line before the event.

## A tightening Senate race

The rally is aimed at Sen. Darline Graham, the Republican incumbent in a contest against Democrat Annie Andrews. Fox News reported that the race has tightened as Election Day approaches, which prompted Trump to return to the state. Fox also reported that former President Barack Obama rallied Democrats in Georgia on the same day, while Trump campaigned in Ohio.

## Claims about Alaska

At the rally, Trump revisited a controversy over the Alaska Senate ballot, where a candidate with the same name as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan appears. He called it voter fraud and said Democratic candidate Mary Peltola should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. Fox News quoted Trump as saying the other candidate should also be removed. These are the president's allegations. Meridian has not seen a court finding or an official election authority ruling supporting them, and Peltola's campaign has not been quoted in the reports reviewed for this story.

## Democrats on election results

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., told Fox News Digital that Democrats are 'really concerned' Trump may not accept the midterm results if Republicans lose control of Congress. Kelly also said Trump has not ruled out deploying military personnel to polling places, which federal law generally prohibits. The White House has not been quoted in these reports responding to those remarks.

## What to watch

The midterms are next week, and the South Carolina Senate contest and the Alaska ballot dispute are among the races to watch. Meridian will update this story if the campaign, election officials or courts respond to the claims made at the rally.
